skill.name: copytop-signals
skill.description: Read live crypto trading signals, trader intel and alerts from copy.top (top traders on fomo, pump.fun and hyperliquid). Use when the user asks what smart traders are buying, wants to vet a trader or a coin, wants a leaderboard, or wants alerts when several top traders buy the same coin. Read-only, no wallet, no key needed.
skill.summary: Query copy.top for crypto signals, trader profiles, token activity, and cursor-based alerts through its public, read-only service.
skill.author: copydottop

security_audit.summary: All 27 static findings are false positives: Markdown backticks, documented service URLs, and a Dexscreener profile reference. The instructions describe read-only queries, require user confirmation for orders, and warn that market figures are not advice. No evidence found of credential theft, data exfiltration, destructive commands, or prompt injection in the supplied file; remote service behavior was not verified.

content.user_title: Research Crypto Signals and Trader Activity
content.value_statement: Crypto signals need context from trader history, token holders, and recent activity. This skill guides read-only copy.top queries to compare signals and track alerts.
actual_capabilities: Resolve names, handles, tickers, and addresses before requesting trader or token details.
Retrieve hot coins, recent trades, attention rankings, money flows, and Dexscreener profile payment activity.
Compare trader leaderboards and inspect profit, return, win rate, fair play status, positions, and trading theses.
Inspect token price, market capitalization, holders, sellers, and whether tracked top traders still hold a position.
Retrieve incremental alerts using cursors and filters for trader count, trade size, and market capitalization.
Provide returned trader and token links for actions that users confirm separately on copy.top.
limitations: Requires access to the external copy.top service through MCP or HTTP; service behavior and data accuracy were not independently verified.
The documented service is read-only and cannot access private accounts or place orders.
Unauthenticated access allows 20 calls per minute; search, get_trader, and get_token each have a documented six-call limit.
Market figures are not financial advice, and historical performance does not predict future results.

use_cases.title: Evaluate a new token signal
use_cases.description: Compare a hot coin with its holder activity, early buyers, and fair play indicators before making an independent decision.

use_cases.title: Compare trader track records
use_cases.description: Review ranked traders, returns, win rates, open positions, and written theses across supported leaderboard platforms.

use_cases.title: Track changes in market activity
use_cases.description: Use cursor-based alerts to follow trader confluence and large trades while retaining state between checks.

prompt_templates.title: Review current hot coins
prompt_templates.prompt: Show coins tracked traders bought during the last hour. Include available market capitalization and returned source links. Do not recommend purchases.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a trader
prompt_templates.prompt: Resolve [trader handle] with search. Summarize performance, fair play status, open positions, and recent trades. Include the returned trader link.

prompt_templates.title: Cross-check a token signal
prompt_templates.prompt: Resolve [token name or address]. Review holders, sellers, and early buyers. Check buyer fair play and whether top traders remain invested.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: compare token activity with trader history.

prompt_templates.title: Continue filtered alert checks
prompt_templates.prompt: Fetch alerts using [saved cursor], [minimum top traders], [minimum trade size], and [maximum market cap]. Return new events and the updated cursor.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: perform incremental monitoring while respecting request limits.

output_examples.input: What would a token signal review include?
output: Illustrative report structure, not live market data.
Identity: resolved chain and token address.
Activity: recent buyers, sellers, and tracked traders still holding.
Context: early buyer performance and fair play status.
Reference: the token link returned by the service.
Caution: market figures are not advice, and past performance does not predict results.

output_examples.input: How would an incremental alert check be summarized?
output: Illustrative summary structure, not an actual alert response.
Scope: new events after the saved cursor using the requested filters.
Events: trader confluence, large trades, or thesis updates returned by the service.
Continuation: retain the returned cursor for the next check.
Timing: wait about one minute before the next request.

best_practices: Resolve identifiers with search and use returned handles, chains, and addresses instead of guessing.
Cross-check token activity with trader fair play status and whether top traders still hold positions.
Retain alert cursors, respect request limits, and keep every trading decision under user control.
anti_patterns: Treating attention scores or historical returns as guaranteed investment outcomes.
Repeating full alert queries without a saved cursor or polling beyond documented request limits.
Inventing token addresses or attempting to place orders through a read-only research service.

faq.question: Does this skill need a wallet or API key?
faq.answer: The documented public service requires neither a wallet nor an API key for access within its unauthenticated limits.

faq.question: Can this skill buy tokens or copy trades automatically?
faq.answer: No. It retrieves information and provides returned links. Users confirm orders separately on copy.top.

faq.question: How does it connect to copy.top?
faq.answer: It documents the copy.top HTTPS MCP endpoint and a direct HTTP request example for clients without MCP support.

faq.question: Which trader platforms are described?
faq.answer: The skill describes fomo, pump.fun, and Hyperliquid tracking. Its leaderboard documentation explicitly lists fomo and pumpfun platform filters.

faq.question: How are repeated alerts handled?
faq.answer: Save the returned cursor and pass it as since on the next request. The skill recommends checking about once per minute.

faq.question: Are signals financial advice or guaranteed results?
faq.answer: No. The skill explicitly treats figures as data, not advice, and states that past performance does not predict results.
